story.title: The Cottage at Midnight
story.subtitle: A private art restitution meeting conceals a map of postwar intelligence debts.
story.premise: collector Margot Bellier's confidential restitution meeting for a painting called Midnight Cottage brings five accomplished strangers to a house in Grambois. Each accepted a different private promise from Margot Bellier; one came to make sure that promise could never be kept.

characters.privateIdentity: Your client is your own family, concealed to preserve professional credibility.
characters.privateObjective: Secure lawful restitution without revealing your personal stake too early.

solutionSteps.title: Restitution denied

host.name: Margot Bellier
host.title: Margot Bellier, collector and former courier; then Game Master

story.solutionSummary: Olivier’s father sold the safe-house chain to the occupiers and later acquired the painting to suppress the record. Margot planned to return it with a decoded provenance. Olivier killed her and cast the dispute as competing ownership claims. The guests’ memories independently connect his family archive to the hidden map.

clues.text: The painted windows correspond to safe-house numbers, not artistic perspective.
Olivier’s family inventory describes the work before its alleged purchase date.
Margot invited claimants, witnesses, and a decoder rather than ordinary buyers.
The real cottage matches a detail painted over after the war.
Olivier knew which safe house was betrayed before the code was explained.
